note: Original spellings and glosses are preserved as supplied. Editorial entries below distinguish meaning, register and attested regional scope; contributor origin is not inferred.

editorialEntries.scope: General Spanish reference; listed availability does not claim country-specific frequency or local endorsement.
editorialEntries.note: The source gloss is ass. Arse is the corresponding British spelling for the vulgar body-part sense; buttocks is neutral. Object-bottom and idiomatic uses require context.
editorialEntries.sourceName: RAE · Diccionario de la lengua española

editorialEntries.us: dick / cock; neutral clinical word: penis
editorialEntries.uk: dick / cock; neutral clinical word: penis
editorialEntries.note: The source gloss is cock. This anatomical sense is separate from the sailing spar and fixed expressions such as me vale verga. A full sentence determines the reading.
editorialEntries.sourceName: RAE · Diccionario de la lengua española

editorialEntries.scope: ASALE anatomical sense attested in Ecuador, Mexico, Costa Rica, Cuba, Puerto Rico, Colombia, Honduras and El Salvador. Other senses and countries need separate context.
editorialEntries.note: The source gloss is pussy. ASALE records the vulva sense in Ecuador and several other countries. Panocha can also name foods or sugar; Bolivia has a documented corn-cake sense. Do not assume every use is anatomical or translate it as the internal vagina.

editorialEntries.scope: General Spanish reference; listed availability does not claim country-specific frequency or local endorsement.
editorialEntries.note: The source gloss is bitch; it can fit an insult in context, but is not universal. The noun can mean whore, while sex worker is neutral wording with a different register. Exclamations and intensifiers need separate translation; never replace puta mechanically inside a sentence.
editorialEntries.sourceName: RAE · Diccionario de la lengua española

editorialEntries.scope: General Spanish reference; listed availability does not claim country-specific frequency or local endorsement.
editorialEntries.note: The source gloss effeminate describes gender expression. It can be disparaging when applied to someone. This entry does not infer sexual orientation and does not treat gay as an automatic equivalent.
editorialEntries.sourceName: RAE · Diccionario de la lengua española

editorialEntries.scope: ASALE contemptuous-person sense attested in Ecuador, Bolivia, Venezuela, Colombia, Peru and Cuba, among other countries.
editorialEntries.note: The source spells this mal parido; the dictionary headword is malparido. Bastard is a possible English insult, not a claim about parentage. Force depends on speaker and context. The literal participle of malparir is a separate grammatical reading.
